title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
claim: One model accepts any amount of partial input, from sparse to rich, and always outputs a complete joint scene representation.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right: stacked input rows, central model box, output panel
description: The figure has three parts, read left to right. On the left, under the heading 'Input conditioning spectrum', four color-coded rounded rows are stacked. They are Text Prompt (a speech bubble describing a living room), First-Last RGB + Camera, Full RGB sequence, and RGB + Depth + Camera. Each row shows thumbnails of a room, depth maps and a 3D camera trajectory plot. A vertical arrow on the far left runs from 'Less' to 'More' observed information. Gray arrows lead to a central gradient-filled rounded box labeled 'Unified Generative Geometry Model' with the note 'Jointly models RGB, Depth, Camera'. Another arrow leads to the right panel, 'Complete scene representation'. That panel shows a full RGB sequence, a full depth sequence in rainbow colormap, and a camera trajectory plot.
caption: A unified model for generation and prediction. We formulate visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion in a single joint model over RGB, depth, and camera pose. Given arbitrary partial observations, ranging from a text prompt to RGB sequences with geometric cues, our model jointly uses these modalities to infer a complete 4D scene representation, enabling both generation from sparse inputs and geometric prediction from observations.
abstract: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations. Furthermore, our generative formulation enables inference-time search over multiple plausible scene hypotheses, using geometric evidence extracted from observed RGB frames to improve geometric prediction without ground truth geometry. We demonstrate UGG's effectiveness over non-unified baselines across camera-controlled video generation, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction, including in challenging sparse observation settings. Code and visualizations are available at https://ugg-model.github.io/
